exposure: Intrauterine carbamazepine (CBZ) exposure (10 mg/kg/day, 25 mg/kg/day, 50 mg/kg/day)
cohort: The study included 24 female Wistar pregnant rats, 20 weeks old with an average body weight of 150-200g, and their fetuses.
finding: Intrauterine carbamazepine exposure negatively affected fetal bone ossification and growth in a dose-dependent manner, resulting in loss of ossification areas, decreased calcium concentration, thinned cartilage matrix, and reduced TRAP and AP expression.
